result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, but lacks basic safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or lane markings. The environment is characterized by older residential and mixed-use buildings with some vacant lots and visible sidewalk debris.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks any painted crosswalks, providing no designated or protected space for pedestrians to cross.

hazards.name: Absence of lane markings
hazards.description: The lack of center lines or lane markings can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning and higher speeds.

hazards.name: Sidewalk debris and poor maintenance
hazards.description: Trash and uneven pavement on the right-hand sidewalk create minor trip hazards and may discourage use.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Roadway Striping
interventions.description: Add center line and parking lane markings to organize traffic flow and narrow the perceived travel lane width.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to reduce pedestrian crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a narrow sidewalk directly adjacent to residential buildings with no buffer from the roadway. The walkway is significantly degraded by litter, debris, and uneven surfaces, creating tripping hazards and a neglected atmosphere.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Large trash bags and loose litter are scattered across the walkway, forcing pedestrians to deviate from their path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and right foreground on the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven sidewalk surfaces create potential tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Visible across the entire foreground sidewalk area.

interventions.title: Enhanced Maintenance and Sanitation
interventions.description: Establish a regular schedule for trash removal and sidewalk cleaning to keep the walkway clear of debris.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair or replace damaged concrete sections to ensure a smooth, level walking surface.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Install street trees or planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the street.

result.summary: The street features sidewalks on both sides, but lacks marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures. The environment is a mix of residential buildings and open space, with on-street parking creating potential sightline obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked crossing points visible for pedestrians to safely traverse the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: A line of parked cars on the right side of the street can obscure pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: Utility pole obstruction
hazards.description: Utility poles are located within the paved walkway area on the left, narrowing the clear path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint to designate safe crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Install speed humps or cushions to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential/mixed-use context.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a continuous paved sidewalk and a mix of row houses and a fenced vacant lot. While the environment is generally walkable, the sidewalk lacks a buffer from the roadway and contains a signpost that may obstruct movement for some users.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A signpost is located in the middle of the sidewalk, reducing the effective clear width for pedestrians with mobility aids or strollers.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb with no physical separation or planting strip from moving traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire visible length of the sidewalk.

interventions.title: Relocate Signage
interventions.description: Move the signpost to the edge of the sidewalk or a furniture zone to clear the primary walking path.

interventions.title: Install Curb Extensions or Planters
interventions.description: Add a furniture zone or planting strip between the sidewalk and the street to provide a safety buffer and improve the pedestrian experience.
